title: Holding, separate opinion, and doctrinal development
shortTitle: Holding, separate opinion, and doctrinal development
summary: A precedent’s contribution depends on what the court decided, the facts and posture before it, and which reasoning commanded the necessary votes. A dissent or concurrence can illuminate a dispute without becoming the holding of the Court.
notes: The casebook edits opinions and includes commentary.

sections.Meaning: A precedent’s contribution depends on what the court decided, the facts and posture before it, and which reasoning commanded the necessary votes. A dissent or concurrence can illuminate a dispute without becoming the holding of the Court.
sections.How to work through the question: Read the disposition and the controlling parts of the opinion. Identify any issues expressly reserved. Compare later assigned decisions that adopt, distinguish, narrow, or reject earlier formulations. A case appearing later in the syllabus is not necessarily a later decision.

learning.coverage: Editorial synthesis of the cited assigned reading; inspect the cases for facts and qualifications.
